status: Bank-specific scenario estimates using shared macro v1 (fingerprint b3c4412d681469e8d974e0c067af8e28435f5669900a9f1b4c54b0178992b8df); regulatory threshold 13% and CRR 20% taken from the shared macro file; not investment advice.

anchor.method: Use the observed 30 Sep 2026 bank balance sheet and the year-to-date bank income statement. Q4 is estimated from the 9M run rate with a scenario multiplier. 9M gross loans and allowance are not disclosed: estimate 9M gross from 9M net using the FY2025 reported allowance/gross ratio (6.31%), then allowance = gross - net as an estimate. No historical imputation.

loan_growth.method: 2027 onward nominal GDP approximation = shared real GDP growth + CPI inflation, plus a bank-specific spread in percentage points; 2026 Q4 net loan growth applied to the September actual. Annual growth capped/floored at -10% and 35%.
loan_growth.reason: Bank gross loans grew 12.1% FY2021, 13.3% FY2022, 23.1% FY2023, 23.7% FY2024 and 13.0% FY2025. September-2026 net loans 4,027.925m vs FY2025 net 3,457.667m is a strong 9M run-rate; assume growth normalises toward nominal GDP plus a modest spread.

deposit_growth.method: Nominal GDP approximation plus spread; 2026 Q4 from the September deposit balance.
deposit_growth.reason: Bank customer deposits rose sharply to FY2024 and FY2025 (6,114.923m, 8,368.068m) but fell in the nine months to Sep-2026 to 7,222.033m as the Bank shifted to wholesale borrowing (2,767.292m at Sep-2026 vs 2,091.662m at FY2025). Assume Q4 recovery and then growth normalising toward nominal GDP.

investment_yield.method: Securities yield starts at the FY2025 note-8 IMPLIED yield on the amortised-cost (unpledged + pledged) securities book and reprises only PARTIALLY toward the shared 364-day T-bill rate (proportional pass-through beta, see model.py Y25_IMPL/PASSTHRU). FVTPL securities are EXCLUDED (their return is in the net FVTPL line).
investment_yield.reason: The Bank's amortised-cost securities book is largely held to maturity, so its yield is locked near its purchase level; full pass-through to the current bill rate would be unrealistic. The FY2025 implied securities yield and the partial-repricing betas are shown in checks.md.

loan_yield.method: Loan yield starts at the FY2025 note-8 IMPLIED yield on average gross loans and reprises only PARTIALLY toward the shared policy rate (proportional pass-through beta, see model.py Y25_IMPL/PASSTHRU).
loan_yield.reason: The FY2025 note-8 interest income on loans (506.986m) on average gross loans of ~3,477m implies an effective loan yield of about 14.6%, well below the 18% policy rate and the 22.22% average lending rate; much of the book is fixed/slow-repricing, so the model anchors on that implied level and reprises only partially as the policy rate falls. The implied level, the pass-through beta and the resulting path are shown in checks.md.

cash_yield_factor.method: Cash and BoG balances yield starts at the FY2025 note-8 IMPLIED cash yield and reprises only PARTIALLY toward the shared policy rate (proportional pass-through beta). The earning cash base EXCLUDES the CRR-proxy reserve (non-earning).
cash_yield_factor.reason: The Bank holds a very large cash and BoG balance (6,033.188m at FY2025, 45-50% of assets) that earns a low yield relative to the policy rate; the FY2025 implied cash yield anchors the path.

cost_of_funds.method: Split funding cost. Customer deposits and wholesale funding (due to banks + borrowings + bonds) are priced SEPARATELY: each starts at its FY2025 note-9 IMPLIED cost and reprises only PARTIALLY toward the shared policy rate (proportional pass-through beta, see model.py Y25_IMPL/PASSTHRU). The blended x_cost_of_funds_pct is the balance-weighted average for reporting only.
cost_of_funds.reason: FY2025 note-9 (printed p.106) splits interest expense into deposits from banks 3.683m, customer deposits 227.208m, debt securities 18.376m, borrowed funds 288.265m and lease 0.600m (total 538.132m). Borrowed funds alone are 288.265m and grew from 214.897m in FY2024, so a single blended factor hides materially cheaper customer deposits against much more expensive wholesale funding. The split matters because the Bank has shifted toward wholesale funding (borrowings 2,767.292m at 9M-2026 vs 2,091.662m at FY2025). Wholesale repricing is a sensitivity via the policy-rate pass-through on the note-9 wholesale factor.

fee_growth.method: Shared nominal GDP proxy plus spread; preserve the fee expense/income ratio unless stress applied.
fee_growth.reason: Fee and commission income grew from 93.477m (FY2024) to 107.619m (FY2025), about 15%.

opex_growth.method: Shared CPI inflation plus a percentage-point spread.
opex_growth.reason: Personnel and other operating expenses grew in FY2025; inflation plus a growth-related overhead is a transparent sensitivity, not guidance.

cost_of_risk.method: Loan impairment charge / average gross loans; scenario percentage. Floor modelled impairment at the increase in allowance stock to prevent an unfunded allowance build.
cost_of_risk.reason: FY2025 net loan impairment was 20.696m on average gross loans near 3,477m, about 0.6%; 9M-2026 charge 23.987m annualises to about 0.8%. Base reflects a normalisation upward from a low base; no repeat of the FY2022 DDEP impairment (237.7m) is assumed.

npl_pct.method: 2026 year-end based on the reported 9M 11.60%; subsequent scenario target, not a forecast from loan-level data.

allowance_to_gross_pct.method: Gross loans = net loans / (1 - allowance ratio) at FY2026E; later allowance stock = gross x ratio.
allowance_to_gross_pct.reason: FY2025 reported allowance 232.828m / gross 3,690.495m = 6.31%, matching the reported loan loss provision ratio of 6.31%. 9M-2026 gross/allowance unavailable.

tax_rate_pct.method: Effective tax on positive PBT; no automatic deferred tax benefit for losses.
tax_rate_pct.reason: FY2025 total below-PBT charge 138.260m / PBT 392.850m = 35.2% (income tax 98.976m plus growth & sustainability levy 19.642m plus financial sector recovery levy 19.642m). 25% corporate rate plus levies. Forecast uses a blended 35%; future levy law changes not assumed.

dividend_payout_pct.method: Payout on positive PAT; constrained if distributable retained earnings after the statutory transfer, a capital target or cash minimum is breached.
dividend_payout_pct.reason: The only recent observed dividend is the GHS42.598m paid in 9M-2026 (RB26Q3), about 17% of FY2025 bank PAT 254.590m; no dividend was declared for FY2023 or FY2024 while the Bank rebuilt reserves after the FY2022 loss. Scenario payout sensitivity.

statutory_reserve_transfer_pct.method: Annual transfer from retained earnings (income surplus) to the statutory reserve fund, as a share of positive PAT. An internal equity transfer, so total equity and regulatory capital are unaffected; it caps distributable retained earnings for dividends. The statutory FUND is tracked separately (x_statutory_reserve_fund_fc) so the Act 930 s34 threshold can be tested; the Act 930 s34 band (a function of statutory fund / paid-up capital) is reported as x_statutory_band_transfer / x_statutory_band_pct, a sensitivity.
statutory_reserve_transfer_pct.reason: Source-confirmed 25% of positive PAT: FY2024 transfer 46.926m and FY2025 transfer 63.648m (statement of changes in equity). The FY2025 closing statutory fund was 368.101m and stated capital 401.191m, so the fund is BELOW stated capital; under Bank of Ghana practice (Act 930 s34; the Bank's own policy note, printed p.139) the transfer is 50% while the fund is below 25% of paid-up capital, 37.5% at 25-50%, 25% at 50-75% and 12.5% at 75%+. The Bank actually APPLIED 25% in both FY2024 and FY2025. The base case therefore keeps a CONSERVATIVE 25% policy, explicitly LABELLED as a policy choice and NOT a statutory requirement; the Act 930 s34 band is supplied as a sensitivity. The observed 9M-2026 statutory fund equals the FY2025 closing 368.101m (no transfer in the nine months), so the anchor year adds only the transfer on estimated positive Q4 PAT; the full-year 2026 statutory movement is genuinely unavailable and is not invented.

capital_ratio_target_pct.method: Management buffer (percentage points) above the shared minimum CAR, not an official target; RWA intensity calibrated from the FY2025 audited RWA / assets, then independently flag any minimum shortfall.
capital_ratio_target_pct.reason: FY2025 regulatory capital and RWA are disclosed (CAR 20.15%); 9M-2026 reported CAR 17.83% but no interim RWA/capital breakdown.

q4_income_runrate_multiplier.method: Scale Q4 revenues by the scenario multiplier; Q4 funding expenses multiplied by 1.25 downside / 0.9 upside / 1 base, OPEX 1.10 downside / 1 base / 1 upside, and Q4 risk charge by estimated gross loans and scenario risk / 4; keep the actual 9M flows fixed. Impairment is subject to the allowance-stock floor.

fx.method: The Bank reports a net on-balance-sheet FX position (RB25AR printed p.180) and a 10% currency-move sensitivity (p.182), but the model keeps a central NO-FX-REVALUATION assumption: the balance sheet is not revalued by currency and no incremental FX translation P&L is modelled in the base, downside or upside path. The reported FY2025 exposure and the bounded 10% sensitivity are carried as reference data (x_fx_net_on_bs_eur/usd/gbp and x_fx_sens_pl_*/x_fx_sens_equity_*) and discussed in checks.md, not folded into the forecast.
fx.reason: Not inventing a currency split in the forecast, but not claiming disclosure is absent either. FY2025 bank net on-balance-sheet exposure: EUR -1.262m, USD -14.593m, GBP -1.555m (FY2024 comparatives +0.166m/+16.388m/+1.392m). A 10% move is about -0.126m/-1.437m/-0.156m P&L (total -1.719m if jointly applied) and -0.082m/-0.934m/-0.101m equity (total -1.117m) on the FY2025 position, immaterial against model PAT; the interim currency split is unknown, so the sensitivity is a bounded FY2025 reference only.

cash_reserve.method: Proxy required reserve = scenario CRR x year-end customer deposits. Cash and BoG balances include non-eligible cash, so this is a liquidity screening test, not regulatory compliance.

model_structure.method: Hold non-core balance sheet lines proportional to deposit growth, except property/other assets grow with opex; stated capital and other reserves held constant; securities follow deposit growth; cash balances plug the accounting identity, flagging negative balances or a reserve shortfall without automatically borrowing. Earning base: loans at GROSS carrying amount, amortised-cost securities = unpledged amortised-cost investment securities (note 21c) PLUS pledged assets (note 20, amortised-cost financial assets), and EARNING cash (cash and BoG balances less a CRR-proxy reserve). FVTPL securities are EXCLUDED from the amortised-cost yield (their return sits in the net FVTPL line). Securities/cash yields and deposit/wholesale costs are calibrated from the FY2025 note-8/note-9 split (RB25AR printed pp.106); loans keep the forward policy-plus-spread driver. RWA = gross loans + FY2025 calibrated residual risk intensity x (total assets minus gross loans). Q3 regulatory capital anchored on reported CAR x estimated RWA; Tier 1 capital anchored using the FY2025 Tier 1 / total regulatory capital relationship. Retained profit increments regulatory capital; dividends constrained to pre-dividend cash and the CAR buffer. Report a proxy, not a regulatory return.
model_structure.q4_opex_balance_growth: Annual opex growth divided by four for Q4 property and other assets.
model_structure.allowance_bridge: Implied write-offs/other reductions = opening allowance + modelled impairment - closing allowance; the impairment floor is max(risk-based charge, allowance stock increase, zero). Movements are scenario estimates, not observed write-offs. FY2026 opening allowance is estimated; Q4 only.
model_structure.cash_residual: Do not hide negative cash; show the reserve and funding gap. Cash is the reported cash-and-BoG aggregate, so regulatory compliance is not established.

notes: All numeric driver assumptions are analyst estimates, not reported bank results or management guidance.

The Bank (separate) column is used throughout. The narrative 'NET PROFIT' and 5-year-highlight tables in the annual reports carry BOTH a Bank and a Group column; only the Bank column is used here, never the Group.
2026 income must retain reported 9M results plus separately estimated Q4; model checks must flag any liquidity or capital shortfall.

Shared macro v1 numeric paths are used; canonical macro fingerprint b3c4412d681469e8d974e0c067af8e28435f5669900a9f1b4c54b0178992b8df. Regulatory minimum CAR of 13.0% and CRR of 20% are taken from the shared macro file.
Republic Bank (Ghana) PLC is a Bank (separate) model; Group/consolidated figures are never mixed in.

Note-9 inconsistency: the note prints a net-interest-income subtotal (693.096m FY2025 bank) that disagrees with the face income statement (708.510m). The face statement is used; the note-9 interest-income (1,246.642m) and interest-expense (538.132m) components reconcile to the face figure. Disclosed in checks.md.
The FY2025 ICAAP forward (2026) CAR of 18.11% and the model's FY2026E base CAR proxy are compared in checks.md and are NOT forced to agree: they use different methodologies and dates.

macro_snapshot.note: Use all three shared scenarios; rerun after macro revisions. A missing required driver is a hard error.
